questions.stem: What does NSR 2020 s. 144(1) require of the master before the vessel embarks on a voyage?
options: To obtain written approval of the route from Transport Canada
To plan the voyage only if it is international
To report the route to the nearest MCTS centre
To plan the voyage, taking into account the Annex to IMO Resolution A.893(21), using the required charts and publications
questions.explanation: Section 144(1) requires planning of the voyage before it begins, taking into account the guidelines in the Annex to A.893(21).

questions.stem: Which list gives matters that the route must take into account under s. 144(2)?
options: Crew rosters, fuel prices and port fees
Insurance, cargo value and the owner's schedule
Relevant routing systems, sufficient sea room, known hazards and adverse weather, marine environmental protection measures, and actions that could damage the environment
Only the shortest distance and the cheapest route
questions.explanation: These are the five factors in s. 144(2)(a) to (e). The others are commercial matters that may be part of a business plan but not of the navigation duty.

questions.stem: What does s. 144(3) require during the voyage?
options: Display the route on a required chart, and plot and monitor the position throughout the voyage on that chart
Keep the plan in the company office
Send the position to the owner each hour
Switch off the chart plotter at sea
questions.explanation: The master must display the route on the chart and plot and monitor the vessel's position on it throughout the voyage.

questions.stem: What does s. 146 require before charts and publications are used to plan and execute a voyage?
options: That they be replaced every year
That they be approved by the pilotage authority
That they be correct and up to date from Notices to Mariners or a navigational warning
That they be stamped by the chart dealer
questions.explanation: Section 146(1) puts on the master the duty of correcting charts and publications from Notices to Mariners or a navigational warning.

questions.stem: What are the four stages of voyage planning in IMO Resolution A.893(21)?
options: Departure, passage, arrival and review
Survey, design, build and test
Alert, decide, act and report
Appraisal, planning, execution and monitoring
questions.explanation: The guidelines divide the work into appraisal (gathering and weighing information), planning (the track and plan), execution (carrying it out) and monitoring (checking progress against the plan).

questions.stem: Which statement about the plan under A.893(21) is correct?
options: It covers the whole voyage berth to berth, the master approves it before the voyage, and it is kept available on the bridge
It covers only open water, and the pilot approves it
It is drawn up after departure when weather is known
It is kept ashore and not revised
questions.explanation: The plan covers the voyage berth to berth, including pilotage waters; the master approves it; and it must be available at all times on the bridge for the watchkeepers.

questions.stem: Which of these is a matter that a passage plan should set out under A.893(21)?
options: The crew's shore leave
The method and frequency of position fixing, with primary and secondary methods
The price of fuel at the destination
The name of the vessel's insurer
questions.explanation: Position fixing methods and frequency (primary and secondary), safe speed, under-keel clearance, alteration points and contingency plans are among the safety elements named in the guidelines.

questions.stem: What does MPR s. 213 require of the master?
options: To pilot the vessel personally in restricted waters
To keep a radio watch on channel 16 only
To report every voyage plan to the TSB
To ensure that the intended voyage is planned and that a deck watch is maintained in accordance with the relevant Parts of STCW Code section A-VIII/2
questions.explanation: Section 213 links voyage planning and the keeping of a deck watch to Parts 2, 3 and 3-1 of section A-VIII/2 of the STCW Code (subject to s. 252).

questions.stem: A vessel draws 2.0 m. The master wants 0.6 m under the keel. A shoal is charted at 1.4 m. What height of tide above chart datum is needed to cross?
questions.explanation: Tide needed = draught + clearance - charted depth = 2.0 + 0.6 - 1.4 = 1.2 m. 0.8 omits the clearance, 4.0 adds the charted depth, and 2.6 is the water needed, not the tide.

questions.stem: Low water at 0600 is 0.5 m and high water at 1200 is 3.5 m. A shoal needs at least 1.0 m of tide to cross. By the rule of twelfths, about when is the earliest time the tide reaches 1.0 m?
options: About 0700
About 0800
About 0830
About 0730
questions.explanation: One twelfth of the 3.0 m range is 0.25 m. At 0700 the tide is 0.5 + 0.25 = 0.75 m; at 0800 it is 0.5 + 3 x 0.25 = 1.25 m. It passes 1.0 m halfway between, about 0730. That is the earliest, with no margin, so a real plan would cross later.

questions.stem: Besides the log book, what does the draft Master Limited chartwork competence require you to keep?
options: A record of crew qualifications
A record of fuel purchases
A record of compass errors
A record of tide heights
questions.explanation: The competence includes keeping a log book and a record of compass errors.
